hints: At constant speed, the driving force balances the resistance force ($F_D = 300\text{ N}$).
Use power formula $P = F_D \cdot v$ with $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert Watts to kW by dividing by $1000$.
walkthrough:
At constant speed on a level road, acceleration is zero, so the driving force $F_D$ equals the resistance:
$$F_D = R = 300\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power output using $P = F_D \cdot v$:
$$P = 300 \times 40 = 12000\text{ W} = 12\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: State the equilibrium condition for motion at constant speed:
Because the car travels along a level road at constant speed, its acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $F_D$ exactly balances the total resistance $R$:
$$F_D = R = 300\text{ N}$$

Step 2: State the formula relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Step 3: Substitute the known values $F_D = 300\text{ N}$ and $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 300 \times 40 = 12000\text{ W}$$
The power of the car's engine is $12\text{ kW}$ (or $12000\text{ W}$).

hints: Find 90% of the maximum power: $P = 0.9 \times 12000 = 10800\text{ W}$.
Find the new driving force at speed $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{10800}{25}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $F_D - R = ma$ with $m = 1000\text{ kg}$ and $R = 300\text{ N}$ to find $a$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the operating power at 90% of maximum power:
$$P = 0.9 \times 12000\text{ W} = 10800\text{ W}$$

Determine the new driving force $F_D$ when speed is $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{10800}{25} = 432\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally ($m = 1000\text{ kg}$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = F_D - R = ma \implies 432 - 300 = 1000a$$
$$132 = 1000a \implies a = \frac{132}{1000} = 0.132\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the operating power when the engine runs at 90% of its maximum power:
$$P = 0.90 \times 12000\text{ W} = 10800\text{ W}$$

Step 2: Calculate the new driving force $F_D$ at speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $P = F_D v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{10800}{25} = 432\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction of motion ($m = 1000\text{ kg}$, $R = 300\text{ N}$):
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - R = ma$$
$$432 - 300 = 1000a$$
$$132 = 1000a$$
$$a = \frac{132}{1000} = 0.132\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration of the car is $0.132\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
